subject: Prepay wallet / committed drawdown — structure & ramp schedule
messages: Subject: Initial proposal: prepay + usage drawdown structure

Hi Kevin,

Thanks for taking time with us yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a proposed structure that combines a 12-month prepay wallet with a quarterly drawdown based on actual usage. The high-level points:  - Year 1: $600k prepay (committed wallet) with a 12% term discount off list; quarterly true-ups using the wallet balance; unused wallet credits roll forward within the 12-month term but are reconciled at renewal.  - Optional Year 2: ramp to $1.2M prepay with an incremental 8% loyalty discount (multi-year stacking) and a phased rate card for high-volume token tiers.  - Reporting: daily burn report + monthly reconciliation spreadsheet (sample attached).  - Invoicing: upfront invoice for the prepay with monthly statements showing drawdown.

Two asks from our side: 1) confirmation of the expected usage profile (we included a template DS_expected_usage_by_quarter.xlsx), and 2) whether your procurement needs to see specific language about leftover credits and early termination.

I copied Laura from finance for invoicing details. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20260218_Redwood_Prepay_Proposal_DS.pdf, DS_expected_usage_by_quarter.xlsx
Subject: Re: Initial proposal: prepay + usage drawdown structure

Rishi,

Thanks — this looks like a good starting point. A few clarifying items from procurement:  1) We need the wallet to support a monthly or quarterly drawdown (quarterly is preferred) with visibility into predicted burn so we can budget.  2) For multi-year deals, we prefer an annual prepay instead of a single multi-year prepayment; can we model an annual prepay with an escalator / ramp schedule and a committed minimum for year 2?  3) What happens to unused prepay at renewal or if we under-utilize (e.g., actual usage is 60% of committed)?  4) Any constraints on carry-forward between years?

Also looping in Susan from our procurement/legal — she'll need exact contract language for the prepay wallet and termination clauses. Can you provide a sample clause?

Kevin
Director of Product
DataStream Inc.
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
Subject: Re: Initial proposal: prepay + usage drawdown structure

Kevin — great questions. Quick answers up front:  1) Quarterly drawdown is fine and aligns with our reporting cadence; we can also expose a monthly view for forecasting.  2) We can model annual prepay: Year 1 $600k (12% discount), Year 2 $1.2M (additional 8% loyalty discount) with a 3-quarter ramp schedule (25% / 35% / 40% committed in Q1/Q2/Q3 of Year 2) — this lets you underwrite growth without a single large upfront multi-year payment.  3) Under-utilization: wallet credits are consumed first against actual usage; if usage < committed in a year, any remaining credits can be rolled into a short grace period (60 days) to allow seasonal usage — then they are reconciled. We are open to an alternative where unused credits convert to a one-time renewal credit at 50% value if you prefer a partial refund mechanism.  4) Carry-forward between contract years is limited to the grace window described above; we can extend it with approval (and different discount math).

I've attached an example contract clause in the attached PDF. Laura — can you confirm the invoicing cadence if we do annual prepay with quarterly drawdowns?

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
Subject: Re: Initial proposal: prepay + usage drawdown structure

Kevin / team — from finance: We invoice the full annual prepay upfront (net 30 standard) and then provide monthly/quarterly statements showing consumption against the wallet. For reconciliation:  - If the wallet is consumed at < committed, we show the remaining balance on the renewal proposal. Option A: roll-forward for up to 60 days; Option B: convert unused balance to a renewal credit at 50% value (this is the conservative option).  - If you choose to terminate early, standard early-termination language applies: unused prepay can be subject to a pro-rata refund minus a servicing fee, or converted to a credit if you switch to a different Redwood product. We'll need legal to specify exact percentages.

Please confirm which option (roll-forward vs 50% renewal credit) you prefer — we can mark that in the SOW.

Thanks,
Laura
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
Subject: Re: Initial proposal: prepay + usage drawdown structure

Marissa / Laura — thanks. Procurement's position: annual prepay with a defined ramp for year 2 (we like the 25/35/40 split) and quarterly drawdowns works. For unused credits we prefer the renewal credit at 75% of unused value rather than 50% — DataStream needs predictability and prefers a higher carry-forward value. Also request a clause that allows a 30-day audit of consumption reports and raw usage logs once per year. Can you confirm Redwood supports that?

Also: we will need a sample SOW and the specific clause language for the wallet burn-down and early termination to share with our legal. Can Rishi or Marissa send a redlineable doc?

Susan Park
Procurement Manager
DataStream Inc.
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
Subject: Re: Initial proposal: prepay + usage drawdown structure

Susan — thanks for the clear feedback. We can do the following to keep things moving:  1) Move to annual prepay with the ramped year-2 commit (25/35/40) and quarterly drawdowns for reporting.  2) Change the unused-credit option to a 75% renewal credit (instead of 50%) for this deal, with an audit right once per year for consumption logs (redacted where necessary for privacy/security).  3) We'll provide a redlineable SOW and a wallet/termination clause by EOD tomorrow and share a DocuSign link for signatures once the SOW is agreed.  4) On carry-forward: 60-day automatic grace period, then remaining balance moves to the renewal credit at 75% value.  5) Invoicing: upfront annual invoice (net 30).

Rishi — please attach the SOW and the contract language to the Drive folder and send the DocuSign envelope once legal signs off. Laura — confirm any finance notes you want preserved in the SOW.

Best,
Marissa
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
